label: Pulmonology
blurb: Asthma, COPD, pulmonary hypertension, fibrosis, antihistamines

drugs.name: Albuterol
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapid bronchodilation within minutes
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute asthma exacerbation, rescue therapy, exercise-induced bronchospasm, COPD exacerbation, acute hyperkalemia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle, raising cAMP and causing relaxation and bronchodilation.
drugs.sideEffects: Tremor, tachycardia, palpitations, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, anxiety, headache
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; use with caution in tachyarrhythmias and severe cardiac disease
drugs.tooltip: The rescue inhaler. Beta-2 agonist causing bronchodilation in minutes. Classic Step 1 associations: tremor, tachycardia, and hypokalemia from intracellular potassium shift — which is also why it treats hyperkalemia.

drugs.name: Salmeterol
drugs.primaryEffect: Sustained bronchodilation lasting about 12 hours
drugs.treatmentUsage: Maintenance therapy of asthma (always with an inhaled corticosteroid) and COPD; nocturnal symptom control
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Lipophilic side chain anchors it in the beta-2 receptor membrane domain, producing prolonged beta-2 agonism and bronchodilation with slow onset.
drugs.sideEffects: Tremor, tachycardia, hypokalemia, increased asthma-related death when used as monotherapy
drugs.contraindications: Monotherapy in asthma without an inhaled corticosteroid; acute bronchospasm (slow onset makes it useless as rescue)
drugs.tooltip: Long-acting beta-2 agonist for maintenance, never rescue. High-yield boxed warning: LABA monotherapy in asthma increases asthma-related death, so it must always be paired with an inhaled corticosteroid.

drugs.name: Formoterol
drugs.primaryEffect: Long-acting bronchodilation with rapid onset
drugs.treatmentUsage: Asthma maintenance and reliever therapy combined with budesonide, COPD maintenance
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist with both high potency and rapid onset, raising smooth muscle cAMP for sustained bronchodilation.
drugs.sideEffects: Tremor, palpitations, hypokalemia, headache, muscle cramps
drugs.contraindications: Monotherapy in asthma without an inhaled corticosteroid
drugs.tooltip: LABA that is unusual for having rapid onset, which is why budesonide-formoterol can serve as both maintenance and reliever inhaler in the SMART regimen.

drugs.name: Terbutaline
drugs.primaryEffect: Bronchodilation and uterine smooth muscle relaxation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute bronchospasm; short-term tocolysis to delay preterm labor
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist relaxing bronchial and uterine smooth muscle via cAMP elevation.
drugs.sideEffects: Tremor, tachycardia, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, pulmonary edema with prolonged tocolytic use
drugs.contraindications: Prolonged tocolysis beyond 48 to 72 hours, tachyarrhythmias
drugs.tooltip: Beta-2 agonist notable on Step 1 for the obstetric use: short-term tocolysis in preterm labor. Prolonged use is dangerous, causing maternal pulmonary edema and cardiac events.

drugs.name: Ipratropium
drugs.primaryEffect: Bronchodilation and reduced airway secretions
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute COPD exacerbation, acute severe asthma as add-on to albuterol, rhinorrhea
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively blocks muscarinic M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle, preventing acetylcholine-mediated bronchoconstriction and mucus secretion.
drugs.sideEffects: Dry mouth, bitter taste, cough, urinary retention, blurred vision if sprayed in the eye
drugs.contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, bladder outlet obstruction, hypersensitivity to atropine derivatives
drugs.tooltip: Quaternary ammonium anticholinergic, so it stays in the lung with minimal systemic absorption. First-line bronchodilator in COPD exacerbation, added to albuterol in severe asthma.

drugs.name: Tiotropium
drugs.primaryEffect: Once-daily sustained bronchodilation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Maintenance therapy of COPD, add-on therapy for severe asthma
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds muscarinic receptors with slow dissociation from M3, giving prolonged blockade of cholinergic bronchoconstriction.
drugs.sideEffects: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, increased heart rate
drugs.contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, bladder outlet obstruction, not for acute bronchospasm
drugs.tooltip: Long-acting anticholinergic and a cornerstone of COPD maintenance, where it reduces exacerbations more than LABAs. Kinetic selectivity for M3 over M2 explains the long duration.

drugs.name: Fluticasone (inhaled)
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces airway inflammation and bronchial hyperresponsiveness
drugs.treatmentUsage: First-line controller therapy for persistent asthma; COPD with frequent exacerbations; allergic rhinitis as a nasal spray
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds cytosolic glucocorticoid receptors, inhibiting NF-kB and reducing transcription of inflammatory cytokines while inducing annexin A1 to block phospholipase A2.
drugs.sideEffects: Oral candidiasis, dysphonia, cough, growth suppression in children, adrenal suppression at high doses
drugs.contraindications: Untreated respiratory fungal infection, acute bronchospasm as sole therapy
drugs.tooltip: The single most important asthma controller. Classic Step 1 vignette: hoarseness and white oral plaques from candidiasis, prevented by rinsing the mouth after each use.

drugs.name: Budesonide
drugs.primaryEffect: Local anti-inflammatory effect in the airway
drugs.treatmentUsage: Persistent asthma maintenance, COPD, croup (nebulized), and oral formulations for inflammatory bowel disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist that suppresses inflammatory gene transcription; extensive first-pass metabolism limits systemic exposure.
drugs.sideEffects: Oral thrush, hoarseness, cough, adrenal suppression at high dose
drugs.contraindications: Active untreated respiratory fungal or tuberculous infection
drugs.tooltip: Inhaled corticosteroid with very high first-pass metabolism, so systemic effects are minimal. Also used orally in Crohn disease for the same reason: local action, low systemic steroid burden.

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.primaryEffect: Broad systemic suppression of inflammation and immunity
drugs.treatmentUsage: Moderate to severe asthma exacerbation, COPD exacerbation, sarcoidosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, many autoimmune conditions
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Prodrug converted to prednisolone, which activates glucocorticoid receptors to inhibit NF-kB, reduce cytokine production, and suppress leukocyte recruitment.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperglycemia, weight gain, osteoporosis, immunosuppression, psychosis, cataracts, myopathy, adrenal suppression with abrupt withdrawal
drugs.contraindications: Systemic fungal infection, live vaccine administration; caution in poorly controlled diabetes and active peptic ulcer
drugs.tooltip: Systemic steroid used in short bursts for exacerbations. Step 1 favorites: neutrophilic leukocytosis from demargination, hyperglycemia, and adrenal crisis if stopped abruptly after prolonged use.

drugs.name: Montelukast
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks leukotriene-mediated bronchoconstriction and inflammation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Asthma maintenance, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, exercise-induced bronchospasm, allergic rhinitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively antagonizes the CysLT1 receptor, blocking leukotrienes D4 and E4 from causing bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion, and eosinophil recruitment.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric events including agitation, depression, and suicidal ideation (boxed warning), rarely Churg-Strauss unmasking
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; caution in patients with psychiatric illness; not for acute bronchospasm
drugs.tooltip: Oral CysLT1 blocker, especially useful in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease where COX inhibition shunts arachidonic acid down the leukotriene pathway. Boxed warning for neuropsychiatric effects.

drugs.name: Zileuton
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks synthesis of all leukotrienes
drugs.treatmentUsage: Asthma maintenance, particularly aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits 5-lipoxygenase, preventing conversion of arachidonic acid to leukotriene A4 and thus blocking production of LTB4, LTC4, LTD4, and LTE4.
drugs.sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity with elevated transaminases, headache, myalgia, increased theophylline and warfarin levels
drugs.contraindications: Active liver disease or transaminases above three times the upper limit of normal
drugs.tooltip: Blocks leukotriene synthesis upstream rather than the receptor. Requires liver function monitoring — hepatotoxicity is the reason it is used far less than montelukast.

drugs.name: Cromolyn Sodium
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents mast cell degranulation and mediator release
drugs.treatmentUsage: Asthma prophylaxis (especially in children), exercise-induced bronchospasm prevention, allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis, mastocytosis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks chloride channels in mast cell membranes, preventing calcium influx and degranulation, so histamine and leukotrienes are never released.
drugs.sideEffects: Throat irritation, cough, bad taste, rare bronchospasm; overall extremely well tolerated
drugs.contraindications: Acute bronchospasm; it is purely prophylactic and has no bronchodilator activity
drugs.tooltip: Prophylaxis only — must be taken before exposure and does nothing during an attack. Its outstanding safety profile made it a pediatric favorite, though inhaled steroids are far more effective.

drugs.name: Theophylline
drugs.primaryEffect: Bronchodilation with mild anti-inflammatory and respiratory stimulant effects
drugs.treatmentUsage: Refractory asthma and COPD; rarely used today because of its narrow therapeutic index
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Nonselective phosphodiesterase inhibitor that raises intracellular cAMP, and adenosine receptor antagonist, producing bronchodilation and central respiratory stimulation.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, insomnia, tremor, seizures, life-threatening tachyarrhythmias; toxicity precipitated by CYP1A2 inhibitors such as ciprofloxacin and cimetidine
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled seizure disorder, unstable tachyarrhythmias, concurrent strong CYP1A2 inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: Classic narrow therapeutic index drug. Metabolized by CYP1A2, so ciprofloxacin, cimetidine, or macrolides can precipitate seizures and arrhythmias. Toxicity is treated with beta-blockers and benzodiazepines.

drugs.name: Roflumilast
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces airway inflammation and COPD exacerbation frequency
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe COPD with chronic bronchitis and frequent exacerbations
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-4 in inflammatory cells, raising cAMP and suppressing neutrophil and macrophage activity.
drugs.sideEffects: Weight loss, diarrhea, nausea, headache, insomnia, psychiatric effects including depression and suicidality
drugs.contraindications: Moderate to severe hepatic impairment; caution with history of depression
drugs.tooltip: Anti-inflammatory rather than bronchodilator, reserved for severe COPD with the chronic bronchitis phenotype. Weight loss and psychiatric effects are the characteristic adverse effects.

drugs.name: Omalizumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Removes free IgE and downregulates mast cell IgE receptors
drugs.treatmentUsage: Moderate to severe persistent allergic asthma uncontrolled on inhaled corticosteroids; chronic idiopathic urticaria
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds the Fc region of free IgE, preventing it from attaching to FcepsilonRI receptors on mast cells and basophils, which also downregulates receptor expression.
drugs.sideEffects: Injection site reactions, anaphylaxis (boxed warning), arthralgia, small increase in parasitic infection risk
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; not for acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus
drugs.tooltip: Binds free IgE before it can arm mast cells. Reserved for severe allergic asthma with elevated IgE. Boxed warning for anaphylaxis, so patients are observed after early doses.

drugs.name: Mepolizumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Depletes eosinophils and reduces exacerbations
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe eosinophilic asthma, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, hypereosinophilic syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds interleukin-5, preventing it from engaging the IL-5 receptor on eosinophils, which reduces eosinophil maturation, recruitment, and survival.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, injection site reaction, back pain, herpes zoster reactivation, hypersensitivity reactions
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; not for acute bronchospasm
drugs.tooltip: Anti-IL-5 biologic for the eosinophilic asthma phenotype, selected by peripheral eosinophil count. Remember IL-5 as the eosinophil growth and survival factor.

drugs.name: Dupilumab
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks type 2 inflammation driven by IL-4 and IL-13
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe type 2 asthma, atopic dermatitis, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, eosinophilic esophagitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds the shared IL-4 receptor alpha subunit, simultaneously blocking IL-4 and IL-13 signaling and thus suppressing IgE class switching and type 2 inflammation.
drugs.sideEffects: Injection site reactions, conjunctivitis, transient blood eosinophilia, oral herpes
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; not for acute bronchospasm
drugs.tooltip: Blocks IL-4 receptor alpha, which is shared by IL-4 and IL-13 receptors, so one antibody blocks both. Explains its remarkable efficacy across asthma, eczema, and nasal polyps.

drugs.name: N-Acetylcysteine
drugs.primaryEffect: Liquefies thick mucus and replenishes glutathione
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cystic fibrosis and thick secretions; acetaminophen overdose antidote; prevention of contrast-induced nephropathy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Its free sulfhydryl group cleaves disulfide bonds in mucus glycoproteins, thinning secretions, and serves as a cysteine donor to regenerate hepatic glutathione.
drugs.sideEffects: Rotten egg odor, nausea and vomiting, bronchospasm when inhaled, anaphylactoid reaction with rapid intravenous infusion
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; caution in asthma because of bronchospasm risk
drugs.tooltip: Two high-yield roles from one sulfhydryl group: it breaks mucus disulfide bonds, and it regenerates glutathione to detoxify NAPQI in acetaminophen overdose.

drugs.name: Dornase Alfa
drugs.primaryEffect: Degrades extracellular DNA in purulent airway secretions
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cystic fibrosis to improve pulmonary function and reduce exacerbations
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Recombinant human deoxyribonuclease I that cleaves the extracellular DNA released by degenerating neutrophils, which is the main source of sputum viscosity in cystic fibrosis.
drugs.sideEffects: Voice alteration, pharyngitis, chest pain, rash, conjunctivitis
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products
drugs.tooltip: Cystic fibrosis sputum is viscous largely because dead neutrophils spill DNA into it. Dornase alfa is recombinant DNase that chews up that DNA. Specific to cystic fibrosis.

drugs.name: Ivacaftor
drugs.primaryEffect: Increases chloride transport through defective CFTR channels
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cystic fibrosis with gating mutations such as G551D; combined with correctors for F508del
drugs.mechanismOfAction: CFTR potentiator that increases the open probability of CFTR channels already present at the cell surface, restoring chloride and water secretion.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, elevated transaminases, cataracts in children, upper respiratory symptoms, drug interactions via CYP3A4
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampin, which abolish its effect
drugs.tooltip: A potentiator: it holds open CFTR channels that reached the membrane but will not open. Only works for gating mutations like G551D, which is why CF genotyping guides therapy.

drugs.name: Elexacaftor / Tezacaftor / Ivacaftor
drugs.primaryEffect: Corrects folding and opens CFTR channels in F508del cystic fibrosis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cystic fibrosis in patients with at least one F508del mutation, which is the majority of patients
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Two correctors improve folding and trafficking of misfolded F508del CFTR to the cell surface while ivacaftor potentiates channel opening once it arrives.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, rash, elevated transaminases, cataracts, diarrhea, drug interactions via CYP3A4
drugs.contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment; concurrent strong CYP3A4 inducers
drugs.tooltip: Triple therapy that transformed cystic fibrosis care. Correctors fix the trafficking defect of F508del so the channel reaches the membrane; the potentiator then opens it.

drugs.name: Epoprostenol
drugs.primaryEffect: Potent pulmonary vasodilation and inhibition of platelet aggregation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe pulmonary arterial hypertension, particularly WHO functional class IV
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Synthetic prostacyclin (PGI2) that stimulates IP receptors on vascular smooth muscle, raising cAMP and producing vasodilation and antiplatelet effects.
drugs.sideEffects: Jaw pain, flushing, headache, hypotension, diarrhea, catheter-related bloodstream infection, rebound pulmonary hypertension if infusion stops
drugs.contraindications: Heart failure due to severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
drugs.tooltip: Continuous intravenous prostacyclin for the sickest pulmonary hypertension patients. Half-life is minutes, so abrupt interruption causes life-threatening rebound. Jaw pain is a characteristic clue.

drugs.name: Bosentan
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces pulmonary vascular resistance
drugs.treatmentUsage: Pulmonary arterial hypertension to improve exercise capacity and delay clinical worsening; digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively blocks endothelin-1 at both ETA and ETB receptors, preventing endothelin-mediated pulmonary vasoconstriction and vascular remodeling.
drugs.sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity requiring monthly liver monitoring, peripheral edema, anemia, teratogenicity, decreased sperm count
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), moderate to severe hepatic impairment, concurrent cyclosporine or glyburide
drugs.tooltip: Endothelin-1 is the most potent endogenous vasoconstrictor; bosentan blocks it. Two boxed warnings drive the exam question: hepatotoxicity requiring monthly LFTs, and severe teratogenicity.

drugs.name: Ambrisentan
drugs.primaryEffect: Selective pulmonary vasodilation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, often combined with tadalafil as initial dual therapy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively antagonizes the ETA receptor, blocking endothelin-mediated vasoconstriction while sparing ETB-mediated nitric oxide release.
drugs.sideEffects: Peripheral edema, nasal congestion, anemia, headache, teratogenicity
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
drugs.tooltip: ETA-selective, so it lacks the hepatotoxicity that plagues bosentan and does not require monthly LFTs. Teratogenicity remains an absolute contraindication in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Sildenafil
drugs.primaryEffect: Pulmonary vasodilation through enhanced nitric oxide signaling
drugs.treatmentUsage: Pulmonary arterial hypertension; erectile dysfunction at different dosing
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits phosphodiesterase-5, preventing breakdown of cGMP in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle so nitric oxide signaling is amplified and vasodilation sustained.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, flushing, dyspepsia, blue-tinged vision from PDE6 cross-inhibition, hypotension, priapism, nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent nitrates or riociguat because of life-threatening hypotension
drugs.tooltip: PDE5 inhibition amplifies nitric oxide signaling. The blue-tinged vision comes from cross-inhibition of PDE6 in the retina. Absolutely contraindicated with nitrates.

drugs.name: Riociguat
drugs.primaryEffect: Increases cGMP independently of nitric oxide levels
drugs.treatmentUsage: Pulmonary arterial hypertension and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Directly stimulates soluble guanylate cyclase and also sensitizes it to endogenous nitric oxide, raising cGMP and causing pulmonary vasodilation.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypotension, headache, dizziness, dyspepsia, hemoptysis, teratogenicity
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, concurrent nitrates or PDE5 inhibitors, pulmonary hypertension associated with idiopathic interstitial pneumonias
drugs.tooltip: The only drug approved for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Works upstream of PDE5 by stimulating guanylate cyclase directly — never combine with a PDE5 inhibitor or nitrate.

drugs.name: Pirfenidone
drugs.primaryEffect: Slows decline in forced vital capacity in pulmonary fibrosis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Downregulates TGF-beta and TNF-alpha signaling, reducing fibroblast proliferation and collagen deposition in the lung interstitium.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, anorexia, weight loss, photosensitivity rash, elevated transaminases, fatigue
drugs.contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment or end-stage renal disease
drugs.tooltip: Antifibrotic for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. It slows lung function decline but does not reverse fibrosis. Photosensitivity and gastrointestinal intolerance limit its use.

drugs.name: Nintedanib
drugs.primaryEffect: Slows progression of fibrotic lung disease
drugs.treatmentUsage: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease, progressive fibrosing interstitial lung diseases
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor blocking VEGFR, FGFR, and PDGFR signaling, which suppresses fibroblast proliferation, migration, and differentiation into myofibroblasts.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea (very common), nausea, hepatotoxicity, bleeding risk, arterial thromboembolic events
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, severe hepatic impairment; caution with full anticoagulation
drugs.tooltip: Triple tyrosine kinase inhibitor for pulmonary fibrosis. Diarrhea affects most patients. Because it blocks VEGFR, it carries bleeding and thromboembolic risk like other antiangiogenics.

drugs.name: Beractant (Surfactant)
drugs.primaryEffect: Lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse
drugs.treatmentUsage: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome in premature infants
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Exogenous phospholipid preparation, chiefly dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, that replaces deficient endogenous surfactant and reduces alveolar surface tension per the Law of Laplace.
drugs.sideEffects: Transient bradycardia, oxygen desaturation during instillation, endotracheal tube obstruction, pulmonary hemorrhage
drugs.contraindications: None absolute in the appropriate neonatal setting
drugs.tooltip: Type II pneumocytes make surfactant starting around week 26, which is why premature infants develop respiratory distress syndrome. Antenatal betamethasone accelerates production; surfactant replaces it.

drugs.name: Caffeine Citrate
drugs.primaryEffect: Stimulates the central respiratory drive
drugs.treatmentUsage: Apnea of prematurity; facilitates extubation in preterm neonates
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes central adenosine receptors and inhibits phosphodiesterase, increasing respiratory center sensitivity to carbon dioxide and improving diaphragmatic contractility.
drugs.sideEffects: Tachycardia, jitteriness, feeding intolerance, hyperglycemia, seizures at toxic levels
drugs.contraindications: Necrotizing enterocolitis, cardiac arrhythmias
drugs.tooltip: First-line for apnea of prematurity and one of the few neonatal drugs shown to improve long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes. Adenosine antagonism drives the central respiratory stimulation.

drugs.name: Diphenhydramine
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks histamine-mediated allergic symptoms with marked sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Allergic reactions, anaphylaxis adjunct, motion sickness, insomnia, acute dystonic reactions from antipsychotics
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Reversible inverse agonist at H1 histamine receptors that readily crosses the blood-brain barrier; also has substantial antimuscarinic and antiemetic activity.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, blurred vision, confusion and falls in the elderly
drugs.contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, bladder outlet obstruction, use in elderly patients per Beers criteria
drugs.tooltip: First-generation antihistamines cross into the CNS and have strong antimuscarinic activity — hence sedation, dry mouth, and delirium in elderly patients. Also treats acute dystonia.

drugs.name: Loratadine
drugs.primaryEffect: Relieves allergic symptoms without significant sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, allergic conjunctivitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selective peripheral H1 receptor inverse agonist that is a substrate for P-glycoprotein efflux, so it does not appreciably enter the central nervous system.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, dry mouth, mild fatigue; minimal sedation and minimal anticholinergic effect
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; dose reduction in hepatic impairment
drugs.tooltip: Second-generation antihistamines are non-sedating because P-glycoprotein pumps them back out of the CNS. The tradeoff is that they are useless for insomnia or motion sickness.

drugs.name: Cetirizine
drugs.primaryEffect: Potent relief of allergic symptoms with mild sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Allergic rhinitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, atopic dermatitis pruritus
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist, the active metabolite of hydroxyzine, with limited but not negligible central penetration.
drugs.sideEffects: Mild somnolence (more than loratadine), dry mouth, headache, fatigue
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; dose reduction in renal impairment
drugs.tooltip: The most sedating of the second-generation antihistamines and the most effective for urticaria. It is the active metabolite of hydroxyzine, which explains the residual drowsiness.

drugs.name: Pseudoephedrine
drugs.primaryEffect: Constricts nasal mucosal blood vessels to relieve congestion
drugs.treatmentUsage: Nasal and sinus congestion from upper respiratory infection or allergic rhinitis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Indirect and direct alpha-adrenergic agonist that causes vasoconstriction of nasal mucosal vessels, reducing mucosal edema and airflow obstruction.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypertension, tachycardia, insomnia, restlessness, urinary retention, hemorrhagic stroke at high doses
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, severe coronary artery disease, concurrent MAO inhibitors, narrow-angle glaucoma
drugs.tooltip: Alpha-agonist decongestant. Kept behind the pharmacy counter because it is a methamphetamine precursor. Raises blood pressure, so it is avoided in hypertensive and coronary patients.

drugs.name: Oxymetazoline
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapid topical nasal vasoconstriction
drugs.treatmentUsage: Short-term relief of nasal congestion; topical hemostasis in epistaxis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Direct alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenergic agonist producing intense local vasoconstriction of nasal mucosal vessels.
drugs.sideEffects: Rhinitis medicamentosa (rebound congestion) with use beyond three days, nasal burning, dryness, systemic hypertension if overused
drugs.contraindications: Use longer than three consecutive days; caution in uncontrolled hypertension
drugs.tooltip: Classic Step 1 vignette: a patient whose congestion worsened after weeks of nasal spray use. That is rhinitis medicamentosa, and the treatment is to stop the spray.

drugs.name: Dextromethorphan
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses the cough reflex centrally
drugs.treatmentUsage: Symptomatic relief of nonproductive cough; combined with bupropion for major depressive disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes NMDA receptors and acts as a sigma-1 agonist in the medullary cough center, raising the threshold for the cough reflex without significant opioid analgesia.
drugs.sideEffects: Dizziness, nausea, and at high doses dissociation, hallucinations, and serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors; caution with SSRIs because of serotonin syndrome risk
drugs.tooltip: An NMDA antagonist structurally related to opioids but without analgesia. Abused at high doses for dissociative effects. Serotonin syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs or MAO inhibitors.

drugs.name: Benzonatate
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses cough by peripheral anesthesia of airway receptors
drugs.treatmentUsage: Symptomatic relief of nonproductive cough
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Structurally related to tetracaine, it anesthetizes stretch receptors in the respiratory passages, lungs, and pleura, dampening the afferent limb of the cough reflex.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, headache, nasal congestion; oropharyngeal numbness and laryngospasm if capsules are chewed rather than swallowed
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity to para-aminobenzoic acid anesthetics; must not be chewed
drugs.tooltip: A peripherally acting antitussive, unlike dextromethorphan. Capsules must be swallowed whole — chewing releases the anesthetic in the mouth and can cause laryngospasm and airway compromise.

drugs.name: Guaifenesin
drugs.primaryEffect: Thins airway secretions to make cough more productive
drugs.treatmentUsage: Symptomatic relief of chest congestion and productive cough
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Increases the volume and reduces the viscosity of respiratory tract secretions by stimulating vagal gastric receptors and increasing respiratory tract fluid output.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache; generally very well tolerated
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity
drugs.tooltip: Expectorant rather than antitussive — it makes cough more productive instead of suppressing it. Evidence of benefit is modest, but it is a common distractor on pharmacology questions.

drugs.name: Varenicline
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces nicotine craving and blunts the reward from smoking
drugs.treatmentUsage: Smoking cessation; it is the most effective single pharmacotherapy available
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Partial agonist at the alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor, providing enough dopamine release to reduce withdrawal while blocking nicotine from producing full reward.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea (very common), vivid abnormal dreams, insomnia, headache, neuropsychiatric symptoms, small cardiovascular risk signal
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; caution in serious psychiatric illness and in end-stage renal disease
drugs.tooltip: Partial agonist logic in one drug: enough activation to blunt withdrawal, enough blockade to make a cigarette unrewarding. Vivid dreams and nausea are the signature side effects.

drugs.name: Bupropion
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces nicotine craving and withdrawal symptoms
drugs.treatmentUsage: Smoking cessation; major depressive disorder; seasonal affective disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine and antagonizes nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing craving and withdrawal.
drugs.sideEffects: Insomnia, dry mouth, agitation, headache, seizures at high doses or in predisposed patients, weight loss
drugs.contraindications: Seizure disorder, eating disorders such as bulimia and anorexia, abrupt alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, concurrent MAO inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: Useful when a patient wants to quit smoking and has depression, or wants to avoid weight gain. The exam hook is the seizure threshold: contraindicated in eating disorders and seizure history.

drugs.name: Nicotine Replacement
drugs.primaryEffect: Relieves nicotine withdrawal without tobacco combustion products
drugs.treatmentUsage: Smoking cessation using patch, gum, lozenge, inhaler, or nasal spray
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Provides nicotine to stimulate nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at lower and slower-rising concentrations than smoking, blunting withdrawal while reducing reinforcement.
drugs.sideEffects: Local irritation, insomnia and vivid dreams with the patch, mouth irritation and hiccups with gum, tachycardia, nausea
drugs.contraindications: Immediate post-myocardial infarction period, unstable angina, serious arrhythmias
drugs.tooltip: Combining a long-acting patch with a short-acting form such as gum or lozenge is more effective than either alone, because it covers both baseline withdrawal and breakthrough craving.

drugs.name: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin
drugs.primaryEffect: Restores antiprotease activity in the lung
drugs.treatmentUsage: Emphysema due to severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Purified human alpha-1 antitrypsin augments plasma and lung levels, inhibiting neutrophil elastase so alveolar elastin is protected from proteolytic destruction.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, dizziness, infusion reactions, flu-like symptoms, theoretical infection transmission risk
drugs.contraindications: IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibodies, hypersensitivity
drugs.tooltip: Classic vignette: panacinar emphysema in a young nonsmoker plus liver disease from PiZZ accumulation. Augmentation therapy protects the lung but does nothing for the liver disease.

drugs.name: Methacholine
drugs.primaryEffect: Provokes bronchoconstriction in hyperresponsive airways
drugs.treatmentUsage: Diagnostic bronchoprovocation testing when asthma is suspected but spirometry is normal
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Direct muscarinic M3 receptor agonist on airway smooth muscle that causes bronchoconstriction at much lower doses in hyperresponsive asthmatic airways.
drugs.sideEffects: Bronchospasm, cough, chest tightness, dyspnea; reversed with inhaled albuterol
drugs.contraindications: Severe airflow limitation with FEV1 below 50 percent, recent myocardial infarction or stroke, uncontrolled hypertension
drugs.tooltip: Diagnostic, not therapeutic. A fall in FEV1 of 20 percent or more at low methacholine dose confirms airway hyperresponsiveness. Albuterol is given afterward to reverse the bronchoconstriction.
